s:
A company creates an Amazon API Gateway API and shares the API with an external development

team. The API uses AWS Lambda functions and is deployed to a stage that is named Production. The external development team is the sole consumer of the API. The API experiences sudden increases of usage at specific times, leading to concerns about increased costs. The company needs to limit cost and usage without reworking the Lambda functions. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectivery?
o: Configure the API to send requests to Amazon SQS queues instead of directly to the Lambda functions. Update the Lambda functions to consume messages from the queues and to process the requests. Set up the queues to invoke the Lambda functions when new messages arrive.

Configure provisioned concurrency for each Lambda function. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to register the Lambda functions as targets. Set up scaling schedules to increase and decrease capacity to match changes in API usage.

Create an API Gateway API key and an AWS WAF Regional web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the Production stage. Add a rate-based rule to the web ACL. In the rule, specify the rate limit and a custom request aggregation that uses the X-API-Key header. Share the API key with the external development team.

Create an API Gateway API key and usage plan. Define throttling limits and quotas in the usage plan. Associate the usage plan with the Production stage and the API key. Share the API key with the external development team.

w.y: There is a single known consumer, so an API Gateway usage plan with an API key is the built-in, no-extra-cost way to limit it. The plan sets a throttling rate and burst limit plus a daily, weekly or monthly quota for that key on the Production stage. No Lambda code changes are needed.

o.A: Adding SQS queues means changing the Lambda functions and only buffers requests; it doesn't cap total usage.
o.B: Provisioned concurrency adds cost and does nothing to limit how many requests the consumer sends.
o.C: AWS WAF adds per-request and web ACL charges; a usage plan gives rate limits and quotas at no extra cost.
o.D: Correct: a usage plan with an API key applies throttling and quotas to the external team on the Production stage.

s: Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway
Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway
